# SEO-036: Declare a mobile viewport in the document head

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `metadata` |

| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Every response includes a viewport meta element that maps the layout viewport to the device width, so the page is laid out at the device's own width instead of a desktop default that is then scaled down.

## Rationale

Without the declaration a mobile browser assumes a desktop-width canvas and shrinks the result, which makes text and controls smaller than the platform's own mobile guidance expects.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Add the declaration to the root document template once. Before adding it to a site that has never had one, load the page at a narrow width and check the layout still works, because removing the desktop-scaling fallback changes rendering on every mobile visit.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Read the viewport meta content from the served response and confirm the layout at a narrow viewport width does not overflow horizontally.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `BROWSER`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `viewport-declared`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
